verbs.description: Find what the workspace holds by words What the words find, best first, as `Found` hits: each naming the resource a caller addresses, and only what the caller may read.
verbs.label: Find by words

schema.description: What a search is narrowed to, beside its words: where a thing was said or is kept, and when. Empty, it narrows nothing. What an app tells search about a resource says both, where it has them (a message: the conversation it is in and when it was written). So a search narrowed to one conversation or to last week is answered from what search already holds, and nothing is read through for it.

about.description: What it is, where its app says (`Found::about`): asked with no words, every one of these, the most recent first (the people, agents and conversations a message can go to).

items.description: What kind of thing an entry is, where the app keeps something the shell's generic rows would read poorly: each is its own section, drawn as what it is rather than as a record.

oneOf.description: An agent of the workspace, opened in the conversation it answers in.
A conversation: a channel, a group or a direct message.
One message in a conversation, opened where it sits.
A person or an agent the workspace knows, drawn as themselves.

after.description: From this moment on, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

app.description: What one app publishes alone: a window's search of the app it shows, whether or not the app runs.

before.description: Before this moment, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

place.description: Where: what a result is placed in (a conversation), by its published id or by the id it goes by among its kind.

items.description: One resource a search found, as every caller of the one search reads a result: the resource it is about, what it is, and what it reads as. It crosses the wire as a provider's answer to a search asked over its API (`tilo.search#find`).

about.description: What it is, where its app keeps something more than a record: an agent, a conversation, a message, a person.

oneOf.description: An agent of the workspace, opened in the conversation it answers in.
A conversation: a channel, a group or a direct message.
One message in a conversation, opened where it sits.
A person or an agent the workspace knows, drawn as themselves.

app.description: The app publishing it, when one does: what a caller names it as.

arguments.description: The arguments that open it, by parameter name.

icon.description: The named icon its app gave it (a lucide kebab name).

item.description: Whether it opens as the item its app keeps, which the app draws as its own list draws it.

key.description: The search's own name for the result: where its app published it from and its key there, the same for the same result across searches.

kind.description: Its kind (`tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook`), as its app publishes it.

label.description: Its label, as the person reads it.

locked.description: Whether it is a secret its app keeps locked: nothing of it shows but its app, opened to unlock it (`Found::app`).

open.description: The action a caller runs to open it, when the result is one a caller opens: the resource's own (`open` for one that opens itself, a page's `open-pane`); `None` for a result that is not a resource of an app (a setting, a file, a command) or one reached another way.

people.description: Who it shows, the one in front first (a message's sender, a conversation's people), each by what the workspace calls them now; empty where the caller may read no name for them.

items.description: A person or an agent an entry is about: who a row shows and what it says under its name.

anchor.description: The resource that names them when the record only holds their id (`chat.workspace/people/…`), empty when there is none.

identity.description: Their stable id: picks their colour and their picture.

name.description: The name the record gives them, when it can say it; empty: what their `anchor` is called now.

place.description: Where it is, by what that is called now: the conversation a message sits in.

provider.description: The provider of the record it is in, where the app keeps many records (`record:<app>:<record>`): two PDFs publish their documents under the same id, and only this says which record a result is of.

rank.description: How well it matched, on the ranking's own scale: higher is better.

resource.description: The resource's published id: what a caller addresses it by.

subtitle.description: The line under its label, as its app says it (an entry's subtitle, else the group it lists it under).

when.description: When it was said or happened, in seconds since the Unix epoch, where what its app tells search says so (a message: when it was written).

workspace.description: The workspace it is in, where the search spans every workspace its caller sees (a person's own search); `None` where it is the caller's one workspace.

verbs.description: List the pictures the search holds Every picture the caller may read, as `Picture`: what the device's image model reads to say what each shows.
verbs.label: List the pictures the search holds

items.description: One picture the search holds: the entry an app published that names a picture's bytes.

image.description: The picture's bytes: a content reference in the device's store.

record.description: The record the app publishes it from.

verbs.description: Describe a picture Adds the words a picture was found to show to the entry its app published for it, beside its own.
verbs.label: Describe a picture

schema.description: What a picture was found to show: the words it is found by from now on, beside its own.

picture.description: One picture the search holds: the entry an app published that names a picture's bytes.

image.description: The picture's bytes: a content reference in the device's store.

record.description: The record the app publishes it from.

title.description: What the picture reads as where its app published none.

words.description: The words, each with what a match in it counts.

items.description: One word a picture is found by, and what a match in it counts.

weight.description: What a match in it counts.

oneOf.description: The name a person looks for.
A stable identity typed verbatim: an address, a site, a username.
A secondary line: an author, a sender, a folder.
Other short fields: labels, tags, a subject.
